HD Graphics Using Customized Hardware for Graphic Development

When HD Graphics asked Tech View to tune their workstations for real-time rendering, the brief was blunt: more throughput, no downtime, no exotic maintenance burden. The refresh that followed lifted production throughput by 22% and turned into the case study partners now ask about most.

The engagement started with a thermal audit rather than a shopping list. Tech View instrumented every workstation in the render pool for a week and found the real ceiling was heat soak during afternoon batch runs, not raw GPU capability. Re-ducted airflow and repasted coolers recovered sustained clocks before a single component was purchased.

The GPU pipeline re-mapping came next. Render, preview, and export queues had been sharing cards on a first-come basis; Tech View pinned each workload class to dedicated silicon and sized the cards to the workload instead of buying uniform hardware. Preview latency dropped enough that artists stopped batching their check-ins, which smoothed the whole day's load curve.

Firmware tooling closed the loop. Tech View shipped scripts that snapshot firmware and driver state across the fleet, flag drift, and stage updates during the studio's Friday maintenance window. The HD Graphics team extended those scripts with their own automation routines within a month, which is exactly the kind of ownership the rollout was designed for.

The 22% throughput lift is the headline, but the quieter win is the checklist the study leaves behind: audit heat first, map workloads to silicon second, and automate firmware hygiene before it automates your downtime.
